questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to a limited partnership owned entirely by individuals?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A limited partner may not conduct business with the limited partnership.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A general partner may not be a limited partner at the same time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A general partner may be a creditor of the limited partnership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The limited partnership can be formed with limited liability for all partners.

questions.explanation:
Unlike a general partnership, a limited partnership (LP) provides limited liability to its limited partners. An LP must be managed by one or more general partners, who are jointly and severally liable for the LP's obligations. Therefore, an individual serving as a general partner of an LP has unlimited liability ("The limited partnership can be formed with limited liability for all…").

Much like the managers of a corporation, general partners have a fiduciary duty to the LP and the other partners. This means that a general partner cannot:

compete with the LP.

use the LP's business opportunities for personal gain.

have a conflict of interest with the LP.

conduct LP business in a manner that is reckless, grossly or intentionally negligent, or knowingly violates the law.

A general partner can be a creditor of the LP. However, due to the general partner's fiduciary duty the loan terms must be the same or better than what the LP would receive from a third-party lender.

("A limited partner may not conduct business with the limited partnersh…") A limited partner does not have a fiduciary duty to the LP, or to the other partners, and may conduct business with the LP in the same manner as a third party.

("A general partner may not be a limited partner at the same time.") There are no legal restrictions on owning both a general partner interest and limited partner interest in the same LP.
questions.explanationJa: ジェネラル・パートナーはLPに対して受託者責任を負うが、LPに融資して債権者になることはできる。ただし、その融資条件は第三者の貸し手から受けられる条件と同等以上に有利でなければならない。LPは少なくとも1人のジェネラル・パートナーが経営し、その者は無限責任を負うので、全パートナーが有限責任のLPは作れない。リミテッド・パートナーは受託者責任を負わないので第三者と同様にLPと取引でき、同じLPでジェネラル持分とリミテッド持分を併せ持つことも禁止されていない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.1

questions.stem: Peters owned 500 shares of common stock in Kidsmart, Inc. Accordingly, Peters had the right to

choices.label: A
choices.text: Automatically receive a dividend in any quarter in which the corporation made a profit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inspect the corporate records on demand.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vote for the election and removal of the board of directors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Be a member of the board of directors.

questions.explanation:
A corporation is managed by its board of directors (BOD) and corporate officers, not its shareholders. Even though shareholders own the corporation, they do not manage it. However, they have the right to vote on significant matters affecting the corporation, such as the election and removal of BOD members.

A shareholder may be a BOD member, but ownership of shares in a corporation does not give someone the right to serve on the BOD ("Be a member of the board of directors."). A shareholder, like anyone else, must be elected to the BOD at a shareholder meeting.

("Automatically receive a dividend in any quarter in which the corporat…") Shareholders have a right to receive declared dividends. However, they do not have a right to automatically receive dividends whenever the corporation has a profitable quarter. The decision to declare dividends is made by the BOD.

("Inspect the corporate records on demand.") A shareholder's right to inspect the corporation's records is not an absolute, on-demand right that can be exercised at any time. It's a limited right because the time, place, and purpose of the inspection must be reasonable.
questions.explanationJa: 株主は会社を所有するが経営はしない。それでも、取締役の選任・解任など会社の重要事項について議決権を持つ。配当を受けられるのは取締役会が宣言した場合だけであり、四半期に利益が出れば自動的に受け取れるわけではない。帳簿の閲覧権は、時期・場所・目的が合理的でなければならない限定的な権利である。株主であっても取締役になる権利はなく、株主総会で選任される必要がある。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.2

questions.stem: Two CPAs organized their business as a general partnership. Which of the following advantages may have played a role in their selection of the general partnership form under the Revised Uniform Partnership Act?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The partnership form of business organization allowed them to form their business without the requirement of filing organizational documents with a government agency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The partners' risk of loss from the business is limited to the amount of capital each invested in the business.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The partnership has a perpetual life that is not affected by a partner's expulsion or withdrawal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The partnership can raise capital with sale of common stock.

questions.explanation:
A general partnership is an association between two or more persons or entities to operate a business as co-owners for profit. A general partnership can be created formally (written agreement) or informally (handshake). In either case, the Revised Uniform Partnership Act (RUPA) does not require a general partnership to file a certificate of formation with the partnership's home state. State laws require a more formal creation process for corporations, limited liability companies, and limited partnerships (formation documents, state filing fees).

("The partners' risk of loss from the business is limited to the amount…") General partners have joint and several liability for the contracts and debts made by the partnership with third parties. Therefore, a partner's risk of loss is greater than just the amount of capital contributed to the partnership.

("The partnership has a perpetual life that is not affected by a partne…") Under RUPA, general partnerships have a limited duration. In a two-person partnership, the duration is also uncertain because if one partner withdraws or dies the partnership terminates.

("The partnership can raise capital with sale of common stock.") Corporations can raise capital through the sale of stock; general partnerships do not have stock. Ownership in a general partnership is represented by a capital account maintained in the partnership's accounting records.
questions.explanationJa: 改訂統一パートナーシップ法（RUPA）では、ジェネラル・パートナーシップは書面でも口頭でも成立し、州に設立書類を提出する必要がない。この手軽さが選択理由になりうる。一方、ジェネラル・パートナーは事業の債務に連帯無限責任を負うので、損失が出資額に限定されることはない。存続期間も限られ、2人のパートナーシップでは1人の脱退や死亡で終了する。株式を発行できるのは会社であり、パートナーシップの持分は資本勘定で表される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.3

questions.stem:
Carr, Dunn, Evall, and Farr formed a general partnership. Their written partnership agreement provided that the profits would be divided so that Carr would receive 40%; Dunn, 30%; Evall, 20%; and Farr, 10%. There was no provision for allocating losses. At the end of its first year, the partnership had losses of $275,000. Before losses were allocated, the partners' capital account balances were: Carr, $150,000; Dunn, $110,000; Evall, $85,000; and Farr, $14,000. All partners agreed to contribute cash to restore any deficit capital account balance they may have. Ignore the effects of federal partnership tax law.

After losses were allocated to the partners' capital accounts and all liabilities were paid, and before any deficit capital account balances were restored, the partnership's sole asset was $84,000 in cash. How much would Dunn receive on termination of the partnership?
questions.explanation:
The following four procedures must be performed:

Allocate gains and losses from asset sales based on partner profit and loss percentages.

Partners with a resulting deficit capital account balance contribute cash to restore the balance to $0 (if they have money).

Prorate any unrestored deficit balance among the remaining partners based on their profit and loss percentages. If there are no separately stated loss percentages, use the profit percentages.

Distribute the remaining cash to the partners in the amounts reflected in the final balance of each partner's capital account.

Based on these procedures, the amount of cash distributed to Dunn (and the other partners) is as follows:

Partner | Profit % (a) | Beg cap acct (b) | Loss allocation (c = a × 275,000) | Adj balance (d = b + c) | Deficit partner cash contribution | Final balance and cash (d + e)
Carr | 40% | $150,000 | ($110,000) | $40,000 |  | $40,000
Dunn | 30% | 110,000 | (82,500) | 27,500 |  | 27,500
Evall | 20% | 85,000 | (55,000) | 30,000 |  | 30,000
Farr | 10% | 14,000 | (27,500) | (13,500) | $13,500 | 0
Total | 100% | $359,000 | ($275,000) | $84,000 | $13,500 | $97,500

Dunn will receive a $27,500 cash distribution.

("$0") Farr is the partner who will not receive any cash distribution.

("$23,000") Dunn would receive a distribution of $23,000 if Farr did not restore the $13,500 deficit balance and it was allocated to the remaining partners [ 27,500-30%90%×13,500
questions.explanationJa: 損失の配分割合に定めがないので、利益の割合で損失$275,000を配分する。Carrは$150,000−$110,000＝$40,000、Dunnは$110,000−$82,500＝$27,500、Evallは$85,000−$55,000＝$30,000、Farrは$14,000−$27,500＝−$13,500となる。全員が欠損を補填することに合意しているので、Farrが$13,500を拠出して残高を0にし、現金は$84,000＋$13,500＝$97,500になる。各パートナーは最終資本残高どおりに現金を受け取るので、Dunnの受取額は$27,500である。

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of a limited partnership?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All partners have limited liability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Limited partnerships must have at least one general partner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The death of a limited partner terminates the partnership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limited partnerships are taxed as separate entities for federal tax purposes.

questions.explanation:
Limited partnerships (LPs) are pass-through entities that are not subject to taxation ("Limited partnerships are taxed as separate entities for federal tax p…"). Instead, partners include their shares of partnership income/loss and separately stated items on their own tax returns.

To form an LP, the owners must file a certificate of limited partnership with the appropriate state authority (secretary of state). The LP must have at least one general partner and one limited partner. The general partner is responsible for the management and operations of the partnership and has unlimited liability ("All partners have limited liability."). Limited partners are considered passive investors (like shareholders in a corporation) and have limited liability.

("The death of a limited partner terminates the partnership.") In most cases, the withdrawal of the general partner will terminate an LP. It will continue, however, if allowed by the LP agreement or if all remaining partners agree to do so in writing. The death or withdrawal of a limited partner will not terminate an LP.
questions.explanationJa: LPを設立するには州（州務長官など）にLP設立証明書を提出し、少なくとも1人のジェネラル・パートナーと1人のリミテッド・パートナーが必要である。ジェネラル・パートナーは経営を担い無限責任を負うので、全員が有限責任になることはない。リミテッド・パートナーは受動的な投資家であり、その死亡や脱退でLPは終了しない。また、LPはパススルー事業体であり、連邦税上、独立した課税主体ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.5

questions.stem:
Which of the following facts is (are) generally included in a corporation's articles of incorporation?
Name of registered agent | Number of authorized shares

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
A corporation is formed by filing the articles of incorporation with the appropriate state agency (secretary of state). The corporation is formally created when the state accepts (approves) the articles. Generally, the articles must include the following:

Name: This is the corporation's proposed The state may reject the name if it is already being used by another business entity.

Nature and purpose: This is a description of the corporation's planned business (clothing manufacturer). However, it often includes broader language ("and any other lawful activity") so the corporation can pursue other business opportunities.

Term: The corporation's life can be set for a limited or indefinite duration.

Incorporators: The name and address of each incorporator must be included.

Capitalization: This is a list of the number and types of shares of stock the corporation will be authorized to issue. It is no longer necessary to assign a par value to shares.

Initial board: This is a list of names of people who will serve as board of directors members until the first shareholder meeting.

Registered agent: A registered agent is the person or entity designated to receive notice on behalf of a corporation when it is involved in a legal proceeding. The articles must list the name and address of the registered agent.
questions.explanationJa: 会社は、州の機関（州務長官など）に定款を提出し、受理されることで成立する。定款には一般に、名称、事業目的、存続期間、発起人、発行可能な株式の数と種類（資本構成）、当初の取締役、登録代理人の氏名と住所を記載する。登録代理人は、会社が訴訟に関わったときに会社に代わって通知を受ける者である。よって、登録代理人の氏名も発行可能株式数も定款に記載する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.6

questions.stem: Which of the following actions may a corporation's board of directors take without shareholder approval?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consolidation with one or more corporations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Merger with one or more corporations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Voluntary dissolution.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purchase of 55% of another corporation's stock.

questions.explanation:
Shareholders are the owners of a corporation, but they do not manage it. Instead, a corporation is managed by its board of directors (BOD) and corporate officers. Even though shareholders do not manage the corporation, they still have the right to vote on significant matters that affect the corporation, such as:

Election of BOD members

Dissolution of the corporation ("Voluntary dissolution.")

Mergers and consolidations ("Consolidation with one or more corporations." / "Merger with one or more corporations.")

Amendments to the articles of incorporation

Loans to directors

Liquidating dividends

Consolidations, mergers, and dissolutions are all fundamental changes in a corporation's structure. Purchasing another corporation's stock does not change the corporation's structure and therefore falls within the BOD function of establishing the corporation's strategic direction.

Note: A shareholder may also be a corporate officer or a BOD member, or both. However, when making strategic and operational decisions, that person acts in the capacity of a BOD member or officer, not a shareholder.
questions.explanationJa: 会社は取締役会と役員が経営し、株主は経営しない。ただし、解散、合併・新設合併、定款変更など会社の構造を根本的に変える事項には株主の承認が必要である。他社株式を55%取得することは会社自体の構造を変えるものではなく、会社の戦略方針を決める取締役会の権限に含まれるので、株主の承認なしに行える。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.7

questions.stem: Under the Revised Model Business Corporation Act, which of the following conditions is necessary for a corporation to achieve a successful voluntary dissolution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Successful application to the secretary of state in which the corporation holds its primary place of business.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A recommendation of dissolution by the board of directors and approval by a majority of all shareholders entitled to vote.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Approval by the board of directors of an amendment to the certificate of incorporation calling for the dissolution of the corporation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Unanimous approval of the board of directors and all shareholders entitled to vote on a resolution of voluntary dissolution.

questions.explanation:
Even though shareholders do not manage the corporation, they still have the right to vote on significant matters affecting the corporation, such as:

Election of BOD members

Dissolution of the corporation

Mergers and consolidations

Amendments to the articles of incorporation

Loans to directors

Liquidating dividends

Under the Revised Model Business Corporation Act (RMBCA), a corporation can voluntarily dissolve if there is a recommendation by the BOD to do so and that recommendation is approved by a majority of the shareholders entitled to vote. The RMBCA does not require unanimous approval of the BOD and the shareholders ("Unanimous approval of the board of directors and all shareholders ent…").

("Successful application to the secretary of state in which the corpora…") The RMBCA does not require application to or approval from the secretary of state to voluntarily dissolve a corporation.

("Approval by the board of directors of an amendment to the certificate…") The RMBCA does not require an amendment to the articles of incorporation in order to voluntarily dissolve the corporation.
questions.explanationJa: 改訂模範事業会社法（RMBCA）では、取締役会が解散を勧告し、議決権を持つ株主の過半数がそれを承認すれば、会社は任意解散できる。取締役会と株主の全員一致までは求められていない。州務長官への申請・承認や、解散のための定款変更も必要とされない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.8

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding a general partnership?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Partnership debt must be apportioned based on partnership percentages.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The partnership must file a certificate of formation with its home state.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Partners have unlimited liability for partnership debts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The partnership must remit federal income taxes on behalf of the partners.

questions.explanation:
A general partnership is an association between two or more persons or entities to operate a business as co-owners for profit. A general partnership can be created formally (a written agreement) or informally (a rock band). In either case there is no requirement to file a certificate of formation with the partnership's home state ("The partnership must file a certificate of formation with its home st…"). Corporations, limited liability companies, and limited partnerships require a more formal process for creation (formation documents, state filing fees).

One difference between general partnerships and more formally created entities is that general partners have unlimited liability for partnership debt. In contrast, shareholders in a corporation are not personally liable for the corporation's debts.

("Partnership debt must be apportioned based on partnership percentages.") There are no absolute requirements for how partnership debt will be apportioned among the partners. Absent a contrary agreement among the partners, the debt will be apportioned in accordance with the partnership profit and loss percentages for each partner.

("The partnership must remit federal income taxes on behalf of the part…") For tax purposes, a partnership is considered a pass-through entity and neither pays income taxes nor remits taxes on behalf of the partners. Partners include their share of partnership income/loss and separately stated items on their own income tax returns.
questions.explanationJa: ジェネラル・パートナーは、パートナーシップの債務に無限責任を負う。これは、会社の株主が会社の債務について個人的責任を負わないのと対照的である。ジェネラル・パートナーシップは書面でも非公式にでも成立し、州に設立証明書を提出する必要はない。債務の負担割合に絶対的な決まりはなく、別段の合意がなければ損益分配割合による。また、パススルー事業体なので、パートナーに代わって連邦所得税を納めることもない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.9

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of forming a limited liability company (LLC) as opposed to a partnership?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The entity may avoid taxation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The entity may have multiple owners.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The owners may participate in management while limiting personal liability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The owners may receive allocations and distributions disproportionately.

questions.explanation:
Limited liability companies (LLCs) are hybrid entities that have characteristics of both partnerships and corporations. From a tax standpoint, an LLC can elect to be a pass-through entity (and therefore not be subject to income tax) and be treated like a partnership ("The entity may avoid taxation.").

From a legal standpoint, LLCs provide all owners (members) with the limited liability protection of a corporation. This applies even to members who actively participate in the LLC's business. Limited liability for all owners is an advantage of an LLC as opposed to a partnership, in which some or all owners have unlimited liability.

In a general partnership, all partners are general partners who have unlimited liability for the partnership's debts. In a limited partnership, the limited partners have limited liability, just like members in an LLC. However, a limited partnership is required to have at least one general partner who has unlimited personal liability for the partnership's debts.

("The entity may have multiple owners.") Both partnerships and LLCs can have multiple owners. In fact, by definition, partnerships are required to have at least two owners.

("The owners may receive allocations and distributions disproportionate…") Disproportionate allocations and distributions are allowed in partnerships and LLCs.
questions.explanationJa: LLCはパートナーシップと会社の性質を併せ持ち、経営に積極的に参加するメンバーも含めて、全メンバーが会社と同様の有限責任を受ける。これがパートナーシップに対するLLCの利点である。ジェネラル・パートナーシップでは全員が無限責任を負い、LPでも少なくとも1人のジェネラル・パートナーは無限責任を負う。課税を避けられること（パススルー課税）、複数のオーナーを持てること、不均等な配分・分配ができることは、パートナーシップとLLCの両方に当てはまるので、LLCだけの利点ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.10

questions.stem: The corporate veil is most likely to be pierced and the shareholders held personally liable if

choices.label: A
choices.text: The corporation has elected S corporation status under the Internal Revenue Code.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The shareholders have commingled their personal funds with those of the corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An ultra vires act has been committed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A partnership incorporates its business solely to limit the liability of its partners.

questions.explanation:
One of the primary reasons to form a corporation is to limit the owners' personal liability while operating a business ("A partnership incorporates its business solely to limit the liability…"). This protection is often referred to as a corporate veil because it shields shareholders' personal assets from being used to satisfy the corporation's liabilities. However, courts can pierce the corporate veil and hold shareholders personally liable for the corporation's liabilities in these circumstances:

Undercapitalization: This occurs if the capital the shareholders contributed to form the corporation is inadequate to meet the corporation's reasonable financial needs.

Shareholder fraud: In this situation, shareholders create a corporation with the intent to commit fraud (Ponzi scheme). This is not to be confused with ultra vires acts (unauthorized acts) by directors and officers, which do not result in shareholder liability ("An ultra vires act has been committed.").

Ignoring corporate formalities: This occurs when shareholders operate the corporation without following legal formalities, such as electing a board of directors and holding shareholder and board meetings. In essence, the shareholders act as if the corporation does not exist.

Commingling assets: In this situation, shareholders consistently treat corporate assets as if they were the shareholders' personal assets, using them for personal purposes (paying a home mortgage).

("The corporation has elected S corporation status under the Internal R…") Electing S corporation status is a decision as to how the entity will be taxed. It would not lead to the corporation's veil being pierced.
questions.explanationJa: 会社の法人格（コーポレート・ベール）は、株主の個人財産を会社の債務から守る。ただし、過少資本、詐欺目的の設立、会社の形式（取締役の選任や会議の開催）の無視、資産の混同がある場合は、裁判所が法人格を否認して株主に個人責任を負わせることがある。株主が個人資金と会社資金を混同していれば、法人格否認の典型例に当たる。有限責任を得ることだけを目的とする法人化は正当であり、S法人の選択は課税方法の選択にすぎない。取締役・役員の越権行為（ultra vires）も、株主の責任にはつながらない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.11

questions.stem: Which of the following parties is required to repay an illegal distribution made by a corporation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A director who did not breach a fiduciary duty when approving a distribution from a solvent corporation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A director who did not breach a fiduciary duty when approving a distribution from an insolvent corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A shareholder who did not know a distribution received from a solvent corporation was illegal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A shareholder who did not know a distribution received from an insolvent corporation was illegal.

questions.explanation:
A corporation's board of directors (BOD) determines if and when dividends will be declared and paid to shareholders. Until declaration, the corporation has no liability to the shareholders.

In general, state corporate law prohibits the BOD from declaring a dividend if the corporation is insolvent or if the dividend will render it insolvent. If the corporation is solvent, the BOD may declare any dividend amount up to the higher of the company's retained earnings or current period earnings ("A director who did not breach a fiduciary duty when approving a distr…").

If the BOD wants to declare a dividend that exceeds these amounts, the shareholders must approve the portion that is a return of capital (a liquidating distribution). A dividend distribution that contains a return of capital and is not approved by the shareholders is considered an illegal distribution.

If a corporation pays an illegal dividend, a shareholder may keep it if the shareholder was unaware that it was illegal and if the corporation was solvent ("A shareholder who did not know a distribution received from a solvent…"). Shareholders must repay an illegal distribution they received from an insolvent corporation regardless of whether they knew the distribution was illegal.

("A director who did not breach a fiduciary duty when approving a distr…") A director who declares a dividend when the corporation is or would be rendered insolvent is in breach of a fiduciary duty. However, if the director takes this action based on incorrect information provided by management, the director is not in breach of a fiduciary duty and is not required to repay the illegal dividend.
questions.explanationJa: 州の会社法は、会社が支払不能の場合、または配当によって支払不能になる場合に、取締役会が配当を宣言することを禁じている。違法な配当を受け取った株主は、違法と知らず、かつ会社に支払能力があれば、受け取った配当を保持できる。しかし、支払不能の会社から受け取った違法な分配は、違法と知っていたかどうかにかかわらず返還しなければならない。経営者から誤った情報を受けて宣言した取締役のように、受託者責任に違反していない取締役は返還義務を負わない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.12

questions.stem: Under the Revised Model Business Corporation Act, which of the following statements is correct regarding corporate officers of a public corporation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An officer may not simultaneously serve as a director.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A corporation may be authorized to indemnify its officers for liability incurred in a suit by stockholders.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stockholders always have the right to elect a corporation's officers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An officer of a corporation is required to own at least one share of the corporation's stock.

questions.explanation:
Corporation officers have a fiduciary duty to the corporation and stockholders (ie, owners). This fiduciary responsibility means that the officers must act with a duty of care (honestly, prudently) and with a duty of loyalty. If they honor these duties, then, according to the business judgment rule, they will not be held liable for their good faith errors in judgment.

However, shareholders and other parties may file lawsuits against the corporation and its officers for breach of fiduciary duties of care and loyalty. Accordingly, a corporation's board of directors (BOD) may vote to indemnify (reimburse) officers who are found to be personally liable in a shareholder lawsuit. The BOD must believe that the indemnity is in the best interest of the company. In addition, the indemnity must not be a violation of public policy (indemnification for engaging in illegal activity).

("An officer may not simultaneously serve as a director.") It is common practice for officers to serve on the BOD.

("Stockholders always have the right to elect a corporation's officers.") The shareholders elect the BOD. The BOD then elects the officers.

("An officer of a corporation is required to own at least one share of…") Officers may own shares in the company they manage; however, it is not mandatory.
questions.explanationJa: 役員は会社と株主に対して注意義務と忠実義務を負い、これを守っていれば、経営判断の原則により誠実な判断の誤りについて責任を問われない。ただし、株主などから受託者責任違反で訴えられることはある。その場合、取締役会は、会社の最善の利益になり公序に反しない（違法行為の補償ではない）と判断すれば、株主代表訴訟などで個人責任を負った役員を補償できる。役員が取締役を兼ねることは一般的であり、役員を選任するのは株主ではなく取締役会であり、役員が株式を保有する義務もない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.13

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is a general requirement for the merger of two corporations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The merger plan must be approved unanimously by the stockholders of both corporations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The merger plan must be approved unanimously by the boards of both corporations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The absorbed corporation must amend its articles of incorporation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The stockholders of both corporations must be given due notice of a special meeting, including a copy or summary of the merger plan.

questions.explanation:
General legal requirements for corporate mergers and consolidations

Corporate approval

Majority of members on board of directors of each corporation must approve

Call special shareholder meetings and provide copy of plan

Majority of shareholders of each corporation must approve*

Government approval

File the approved plan with state authorities

State authorities issue certificate of approval

Dissenting shareholders

Dissenting shareholders have right to have their shares appraised and purchased at that price

Short-form mergers (90%-owned subsidiary into a parent) generally do not require shareholder approval.

one legal requirement is that stockholders of both corporations must be given due notice of a special meeting to approve the merger. They must also be provided with a copy or summary of the merger plan. This process ensures that shareholders receive both sufficient notice of the merger and the information they need to make an informed decision.

("The merger plan must be approved unanimously by the stockholders of b…" / "The merger plan must be approved unanimously by the boards of both co…") Mergers and consolidations require approval by a majority, not the unanimous approval, of both the board of directors and shareholders of each corporation.

("The absorbed corporation must amend its articles of incorporation.") When two corporations merge, one (surviving corporation) absorbs all the assets and liabilities of the other (merged corporation). After the merger, the merged (absorbed) corporation no longer exists, and therefore its articles of incorporation are no longer valid.
questions.explanationJa: 合併には、各会社の取締役会の過半数の承認と、株主総会での株主の過半数の承認が必要である（全員一致ではない）。その前提として、両社の株主に臨時株主総会の適切な通知を行い、合併計画の写しまたは要約を提供しなければならない。これにより、株主は十分な情報に基づいて判断できる。吸収される会社は合併後に消滅するので、その定款を変更する必要はない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.14

questions.stem: Which of the following types of business entities permits all of its owners to manage the entity and have limited liability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Joint venture.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Limited partnership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Limited liability partnership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limited liability company.

questions.explanation:
Limited liability companies (LLCs) are hybrid entities that have characteristics of both partnerships and corporations. From a legal standpoint, LLCs provide all owners (members) with the limited liability protection equal to that of a corporation. Basically, an LLC's owners (members) are not personally liable for the debts and obligations of the LLC, similar to shareholders in a corporation. This applies even to members who actively participate in the LLC's business.

A limited liability partnership (LLP) has characteristics of partnerships and corporations. The difference is that in an LLP, a partner has unlimited personal liability for the LLP's liabilities created by that partner's own torts (negligence) ("Limited liability partnership.").

("Joint venture.") Joint ventures share many characteristics with general partnerships, such as unlimited liability that is joint and several for all parties who participate in the joint venture.

("Limited partnership.") In a limited partnership (LP), only limited partners have limited liability. An LP must have at least one general partner, and that person has unlimited liability. In addition, a limited partner who actively manages the LP will be considered a general partner and lose limited liability protection.
questions.explanationJa: LLCでは、経営に積極的に参加するメンバーも含めて、全メンバーが会社の株主と同様の有限責任を受けるので、全オーナーが経営に参加しつつ有限責任を得られる。LLPでは、パートナーは自分自身の不法行為（過失など）による債務について無限責任を負う。ジョイント・ベンチャーはジェネラル・パートナーシップと同じく参加者全員が連帯無限責任を負う。LPでは少なくとも1人のジェネラル・パートナーが無限責任を負い、経営に参加したリミテッド・パートナーは有限責任を失う。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.15

questions.stem: Which of the following partners of a limited liability partnership (LLP) may avoid personal liability when a partner commits a negligent act?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All the partners

choices.label: B
choices.text: The supervisor of the negligent partner

choices.label: C
choices.text: All the partners other than the negligent partner

choices.label: D
choices.text: All the partners other than the supervisor of and the negligent partner

questions.explanation:
A limited liability partnership (LLP) is a type of legal entity that provides some or all of its owners with limited liability. It is like a general partnership; all partners have the right to participate in management of the partnership. LLPs are popular among professionals (CPAs, lawyers) because they provide partners with liability protection from other partners' torts (negligence, malpractice) ("All the partners" / "All the partners other than the negligent partner").

Generally, partners in an LLP are personally liable for their own torts. In addition, supervising partners (a managing partner) are liable for the torts of those they supervise ("The supervisor of the negligent partner"). However, the other partners in the LLP avoid liability for torts committed by other partners.

For example, if a CPA partner in an LLP negligently performs an audit, that CPA is liable for the damages suffered by those harmed by the negligence. If that CPA was supervised by another partner in the firm (the managing partner), that supervising partner is also personally liable for the negligence. However, other partner CPAs in the firm are not personally liable.
questions.explanationJa: LLPは、他のパートナーの不法行為（過失や職務上の過誤）についての責任からパートナーを守るため、CPAや弁護士に好まれる。ただし、パートナーは自分自身の不法行為について個人責任を負い、監督するパートナー（マネージング・パートナーなど）も、監督下の者の不法行為について責任を負う。したがって、個人責任を免れるのは、過失を犯したパートナーとその監督者を除く、その他のパートナーである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.16

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding a limited liability company's operating agreement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It must be filed with a central state agency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It must be in writing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is designed to forestall and resolve disputes among the owners.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is necessary for a limited liability company to exist.

questions.explanation:
An LLC's operating agreement governs relations among the members and between the members and the company, including management, allocation of profits and losses, transfer of interests, and dissociation. Its purpose is to set the rules in advance so that disputes among the owners are avoided or resolved (Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act §§102, 110).

The operating agreement is not filed with a state agency; only the certificate (articles) of organization is filed.
It need not be in writing; under the uniform act it may be oral, implied, in a record, or any combination.
It is not necessary for the LLC to exist; the LLC comes into existence when the certificate of organization is filed, and default statutory rules apply when there is no agreement.
questions.explanationJa:
LLC の運営契約（operating agreement）は、メンバー間やメンバーと会社との関係（経営、損益の配分、持分の譲渡、脱退など）を定めるもので、あらかじめルールを決めておくことでオーナー間の紛争を防ぎ、解決するためのものである。
運営契約は州に届け出ない（届け出るのは設立証書）。書面である必要もなく、口頭や黙示でもよい。LLC は設立証書の届出で成立し、運営契約が無い場合は法律の任意規定が適用されるので、LLC の存在に運営契約は必須ではない。
references: Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act §102
Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act §110
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.21 (AICPA No. 89821)

questions.stem: Under which of the following circumstances would a promoter be relieved of personal liability on contracts entered into while engaged in forming a corporation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the bylaws of the corporation expressly adopt all preincorporation contracts without novation

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the corporation unknowingly accepts the benefits of the contract

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the contracting party verbally agrees to relieve the promoter

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the third party, the corporation, and the promoter enter into an agreement to substitute the corporation for the promoter

questions.explanation:
A promoter who enters into contracts on behalf of a corporation not yet formed is personally liable on those contracts. The promoter remains liable even after the corporation is formed and adopts the contract, unless there is a novation: an agreement among the third party, the corporation, and the promoter that substitutes the corporation for the promoter and releases the promoter.

Adoption of preincorporation contracts by the bylaws makes the corporation liable but does not release the promoter without a novation. A corporation that knowingly accepts benefits of the contract impliedly adopts it, which still would not release the promoter, and unknowing acceptance of benefits does not even create adoption. A verbal agreement by the contracting party alone, without the corporation agreeing to take the promoter's place, is not a novation.
questions.explanationJa:
設立前の会社のために契約した発起人（promoter）はその契約について個人責任を負う。会社が設立されて契約を承認（adoption）しても責任は残り、免責されるのは第三者・会社・発起人の三者が会社を発起人に代えて当事者とする合意（更改：novation）をした場合である。

付属定款で設立前契約を承認しても、会社が責任を負うようになるだけで、更改が無ければ発起人は免責されない。会社が契約の利益を知りながら受ければ黙示の承認になるが、それでも発起人は免責されず、知らずに受けた場合は承認にもならない。相手方が口頭で発起人の免責に同意しただけで、会社が当事者として代わる合意が無ければ更改ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.5 (AICPA No. 90805)

questions.stem: The CPA was preparing the financial statement for a limited liability company. To which of the following would the CPA's report be addressed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Member

choices.label: B
choices.text: Shareholder

choices.label: C
choices.text: General partner

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limited partner

questions.explanation:
The owners of a limited liability company are called members. A CPA's report on an LLC's financial statements is addressed to the entity's owners (and/or its managers or board), so it is addressed to the members.

Shareholders are the owners of a corporation. General partners and limited partners are the owners of a limited partnership (general partners also own general partnerships). None of these terms describes the owners of an LLC.
questions.explanationJa:
LLCの所有者はメンバー（member）と呼ばれる。LLCの財務諸表に対するCPAの報告書は事業体の所有者（または管理者）宛てとなるため、メンバー宛てになる。

株主（shareholder）は株式会社の所有者、無限責任パートナー・有限責任パートナーはリミテッド・パートナーシップの所有者（無限責任パートナーは一般パートナーシップの所有者でもある）を指し、いずれもLLCの所有者を表す用語ではない。
references: Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act §102 (definition of member)
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.20 (AICPA No. 90820)

questions.stem: Two individuals are planning to start a business and need advice on selecting the appropriate form of entity. Their long-term business plan contemplates receiving future in-kind property distributions. Which of the following is a pair of business entities each of which can make a distribution of appreciated property to its owners that would not be taxable to the business entity or to its owners?

choices.label: A
choices.text: C corporation and a limited liability company.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Limited liability company and an S corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: S corporation and a general partnership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: General partnership and a limited liability partnership.

questions.explanation:
Both a general partnership and a limited liability partnership are taxed as partnerships. Under IRC §731(a) and (b), a partnership generally recognizes no gain on a distribution of property, and a partner recognizes gain only if money received exceeds the partner's outside basis; a distribution of appreciated property is therefore generally not taxable to either the entity or the owners.

A C corporation recognizes gain on a distribution of appreciated property under IRC §311(b), and the shareholder has a taxable distribution under §301, so any pair that includes a C corporation fails. An S corporation also recognizes §311(b) gain, which passes through and is taxed to its shareholders, so any pair that includes an S corporation fails as well.
questions.explanationJa:
ジェネラル・パートナーシップとLLPはいずれもパートナーシップとして課税される。IRC §731(a)(b)により、パートナーシップは資産の分配で原則として利益を認識せず、パートナーも受け取った現金が持分の取得価額を超える場合にしか利益を認識しない。したがって含み益のある資産を分配しても、事業体にも所有者にも原則として課税されない。

C法人は含み益資産の分配で§311(b)の利益を認識し、株主にも§301の分配として課税されるため、C法人を含む組合せは誤り。S法人も§311(b)の利益を認識し、それが株主にパススルーされて課税されるため、S法人を含む組合せも誤りである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.6 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: A CPA firm, operated as a general partnership, will dissolve by mutual agreement at the end of the year. During the year, distributions have been made to some partners in excess of their capital invested in the partnership. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the distribution of assets at the end of the partnership's existence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Partners with negative capital accounts must contribute additional funds to the partnership.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Creditors whose debts cannot be satisfied by the partnership assets will have no further recourse

choices.label: C
choices.text: The partnership must engage in additional activity to generate sufficient cash to pay all creditors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bankrupt partners must contribute capital to resolve their bankruptcy proceedings.

questions.explanation:
When a general partnership winds up, its assets are applied first to creditors, and then each partner is entitled to a settlement of its account. A partner whose account is negative must contribute to the partnership an amount equal to the negative balance (RUPA §807(b)). Partners who received distributions in excess of their capital have negative capital accounts and must contribute additional funds.

Creditors whose claims cannot be satisfied from partnership assets still have recourse against the partners, who are jointly and severally liable for partnership obligations (RUPA §306(a)). In winding up, the partnership may only complete existing business; it is not required to engage in additional activity to generate cash. A bankrupt partner's contribution obligation is a claim in that partner's bankruptcy, not a requirement to contribute capital to resolve the bankruptcy.
questions.explanationJa:
ジェネラル・パートナーシップの清算では、資産はまず債権者への弁済に充てられ、その後各パートナーの持分が精算される。持分勘定がマイナスのパートナーは、そのマイナス額をパートナーシップに拠出しなければならない（RUPA §807(b)）。出資額を超える分配を受けたパートナーは持分勘定がマイナスとなり、追加拠出が必要となる。

パートナーシップ資産で弁済しきれない債権者は、パートナーシップの債務について連帯して責任を負うパートナーに請求できる（RUPA §306(a)）ので、救済がなくなるわけではない。清算中は既存の業務を完了させるだけで、現金を得るために追加の事業を行う義務はない。破産したパートナーの拠出義務はその破産手続きにおける債権となるにすぎず、破産を解決するために出資しなければならないという文言は誤り。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.6 (AICPA No. 63809)

questions.stem: A partner in a general partnership is usually not entitled to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To participate in management.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To review accounting records.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To enter into a contract with a third party without the consent of the other partners.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To be liable only for personal negligence.

questions.explanation:
Under the Revised Uniform Partnership Act, all partners of a general partnership are jointly and severally liable for all obligations of the partnership (RUPA §306(a)). A general partner is therefore not entitled to be liable only for his or her own negligence.

Each partner has equal rights to participate in management (RUPA §401(f)) and a right of access to the partnership's books and records (RUPA §403). Each partner is also an agent of the partnership and can bind it to contracts with third parties in the ordinary course of business without the other partners' consent (RUPA §301(1)).
questions.explanationJa:
改正統一パートナーシップ法（RUPA）では、ジェネラル・パートナーシップの全パートナーがパートナーシップの全債務について連帯して責任を負う（RUPA §306(a)）。したがって、自分の過失についてのみ責任を負うという権利はない。

各パートナーは経営に参加する平等な権利（RUPA §401(f)）と帳簿・記録を閲覧する権利（RUPA §403）を持つ。また各パートナーはパートナーシップの代理人であり、通常の業務の範囲内であれば他のパートナーの同意なく第三者と契約してパートナーシップを拘束できる（RUPA §301(1)）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.9 (AICPA No. 73107)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding a shareholder's right to inspect corporate books and records? The right

choices.label: A
choices.text: Is absolute.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Is conditioned upon the demanding shareholder owning at least $5,000 worth of stock.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Requires that the demand to inspect be for a proper purpose.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exists only when fraud or illegality is alleged.

questions.explanation:
Under the Revised Model Business Corporation Act §16.02, a shareholder may inspect and copy corporate books and records upon written demand made in good faith and for a proper purpose, describing the purpose and the records with reasonable particularity, and the records must be directly connected with that purpose. A proper purpose is one reasonably related to the shareholder's interest as a shareholder.

The right is not absolute because it is conditioned on good faith and a proper purpose. The RMBCA does not require ownership of a minimum dollar amount, such as $5,000, of stock. The right does not depend on an allegation of fraud or illegality.
questions.explanationJa:
改正模範事業会社法（RMBCA）§16.02 により、株主は誠実かつ正当な目的のために、目的と対象記録を具体的に記載した書面で請求すれば、会社の帳簿・記録を閲覧・謄写できる。対象の記録はその目的に直接関係するものでなければならない。正当な目的とは、株主としての利益に合理的に関連する目的をいう。

誠実性と正当な目的が条件となるため、絶対的な権利ではない。RMBCA には $5,000 などの最低保有額の要件はない。詐欺や違法行為の主張を前提とする権利でもない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.10 (AICPA No. 60325)

questions.stem: Banner and Smythe merged their competing retail service businesses, each of which previously had been operated as a sole proprietorship. Neither Banner nor Smythe filed any paperwork with the state. They agreed to equally share profits, management rights, and co-ownership rights. What is the status of the merged business?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Joint venture.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Limited partnership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: General partnership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: C corporation.

questions.explanation:
Under the Revised Uniform Partnership Act, the association of two or more persons to carry on as co-owners a business for profit forms a general partnership, whether or not the persons intend to form a partnership (RUPA §202(a)). No state filing is required. Banner and Smythe agreed to share profits, management, and co-ownership of an ongoing business, so the merged business is a general partnership.

A joint venture is formed for a single transaction or limited undertaking, not to carry on an ongoing retail service business. A limited partnership and a C corporation can be created only by filing a certificate of limited partnership or articles of incorporation with the state, and neither Banner nor Smythe filed any paperwork.
questions.explanationJa:
改正統一パートナーシップ法（RUPA §202(a)）では、2人以上が共同所有者として営利事業を営むために結合すれば、パートナーシップを作る意思の有無にかかわらずジェネラル・パートナーシップが成立し、州への届出も不要である。BannerとSmytheは継続的な事業について利益・経営・共同所有を等分に分け合うことに合意しているので、ジェネラル・パートナーシップに当たる。

ジョイント・ベンチャーは単一の取引や限定された事業のための結合であり、継続的な小売サービス業には当たらない。リミテッド・パートナーシップとC法人は州への証明書・定款の提出によってのみ成立するが、本問では何も提出していない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.6 (AICPA No. 63875)

questions.stem: A seven-person partnership lacks a partnership agreement. Under the Revised Uniform Partnership Act, how many votes are required to approve an extraordinary transaction of partnership business?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Four votes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Five votes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Six votes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Seven votes.

questions.explanation:
Under the Revised Uniform Partnership Act, a difference arising as to a matter in the ordinary course of business may be decided by a majority of the partners, but an act outside the ordinary course of business (an extraordinary transaction) and an amendment of the partnership agreement may be undertaken only with the consent of all of the partners (RUPA §401(j)). With seven partners and no partnership agreement to the contrary, all seven votes are required.

Four votes is a simple majority of seven, which suffices only for ordinary-course matters. Five votes and six votes are supermajorities that RUPA does not use for either category of decision.
questions.explanationJa:
改正統一パートナーシップ法（RUPA §401(j)）では、通常業務に関する事項はパートナーの過半数で決められるが、通常業務の範囲外の行為（異例の取引）やパートナーシップ契約の変更には全パートナーの同意が必要である。7人のパートナーがいて別段の契約がないので、7票すべてが必要になる。

4票は7人の単純過半数で、通常業務の事項にしか足りない。5票や6票のような特別多数は、RUPAではどちらの種類の決定にも使われない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.25 (AICPA No. 63867)

questions.stem: A general partnership must

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pay federal income tax

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have two or more partners

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have written articles of partnership

choices.label: D
choices.text: Provide for apportionment of liability for partnership debts

questions.explanation:
Under RUPA §202(a), a partnership is formed by the association of two or more persons to carry on as co-owners a business for profit. Two or more partners is therefore an essential element; a single person cannot be a general partnership.

Paying federal income tax is not required: a partnership is a pass-through entity that files an information return, and the partners, not the partnership, are taxed on its income (IRC §701). Written articles of partnership are not required because a partnership may be formed by an oral agreement or even by conduct, regardless of the parties' intent to form a partnership. Providing for apportionment of liability for partnership debts is not required; if the agreement is silent, RUPA's default rules apply, and all partners are jointly and severally liable for partnership obligations (RUPA §306).
questions.explanationJa:
RUPA §202(a) により、パートナーシップは「2人以上の者が共同所有者として営利事業を営む団体」として成立します。したがって2人以上のパートナーが必須で、1人だけでは一般パートナーシップになりません。

連邦所得税の納付は不要です。パートナーシップはパススルー事業体で、情報申告書を提出するだけで、課税されるのは各パートナーです（IRC §701）。書面のパートナーシップ契約書も不要で、口頭の合意や行動からでも成立します。債務の負担割合の定めも不要で、定めが無ければ RUPA の任意規定が適用され、パートナーは全員が連帯して責任を負います（RUPA §306）。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.1

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the differences and similarities between a corporation and a limited partnership?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Directors owe fiduciary duties to the corporation and limited partners owe such duties to the partnership.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A corporation and a limited partnership may be created only pursuant to a state statute, and a copy of its organizational document must be filed with the proper state agency.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shareholders may be entitled to vote on corporate matters, whereas limited partners are prohibited from voting on any partnership matters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stock of a corporation may be subject to the federal securities laws registration requirements, whereas limited partnership interests are automatically exempt from such requirements.

questions.explanation:
Both entities are creatures of state statute. A corporation comes into existence only when its articles of incorporation are filed with the secretary of state (RMBCA §2.01–§2.03), and a limited partnership is formed only when a certificate of limited partnership is filed with the state (ULPA (2001) §201). A general partnership, by contrast, needs no filing.

The statement that limited partners owe fiduciary duties to the partnership is wrong: under ULPA (2001) §305, a limited partner does not have any fiduciary duty to the partnership or other partners solely by reason of being a limited partner (directors, however, do owe fiduciary duties to the corporation). The statement that limited partners are prohibited from voting on any partnership matters is wrong because limited partners do vote on certain matters, such as amending the partnership agreement (ULPA (2001) §406(b)) or admitting new partners (ULPA (2001) §401). The statement that limited partnership interests are automatically exempt from securities registration is wrong; limited partnership interests are generally investment contracts and therefore securities, so they are subject to registration unless an exemption applies.
questions.explanationJa:
株式会社もリミテッド・パートナーシップ（LP）も、州法に基づいてのみ設立でき、設立書類の州への提出が必要です。株式会社は定款（articles of incorporation）を州務長官に提出して成立し（RMBCA §2.01〜§2.03）、LP は certificate of limited partnership を州に提出して成立します（ULPA (2001) §201）。一般パートナーシップは提出不要である点と対照的です。

「有限責任パートナーもパートナーシップに信認義務を負う」は誤りです。ULPA (2001) §305 により、有限責任パートナーであるというだけでは信認義務を負いません（取締役は会社に信認義務を負います）。「有限責任パートナーはいかなる事項にも議決権が無い」も誤りで、契約の変更（§406(b)）や新パートナーの加入（§401）などには同意権があります。「LP の持分は証券登録規制が自動的に免除される」も誤りで、LP 持分は一般に投資契約として証券に当たり、免除規定に該当しない限り登録が必要です。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.2

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the effect of the assignment of an interest in a general partnership?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The assignee becomes a partner.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The assignee is responsible for a proportionate share of past and future partnership debts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The assignment automatically dissolves the partnership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The assignment transfers the assignor's interest in partnership profits and surplus.

questions.explanation:
Under RUPA §502–§503, a partner's transferable interest consists only of the partner's share of profits and losses and the right to receive distributions. A transfer of that interest entitles the transferee to receive the distributions the transferor would otherwise receive, so the assignment transfers the assignor's interest in partnership profits and surplus.

The assignee does not become a partner; a transferee has no right to participate in management or to inspect records, and becomes a partner only with the consent of all the other partners (RUPA §401(i), §503(a)(3)). The assignee is not responsible for past or future partnership debts, because liability attaches to partners and the assignee is not a partner; the assignor remains a partner and remains liable. The assignment does not dissolve the partnership; RUPA §503(a)(2) states that a transfer does not by itself cause the partner's dissociation or a dissolution and winding up of the partnership business.
questions.explanationJa:
RUPA §502〜§503 により、パートナーが譲渡できる持分は「損益の分配を受ける権利と分配金を受け取る権利」だけです。持分を譲渡すると、譲受人は譲渡人が受け取るはずだった分配を受け取れるようになります。つまり、譲渡によって移転するのは利益と残余財産に対する権利です。

譲受人はパートナーにはなりません。経営に参加する権利や帳簿閲覧権は無く、他の全パートナーの同意があって初めてパートナーになります（§401(i)）。譲受人はパートナーではないため、過去・将来のパートナーシップ債務の責任も負いません（譲渡人はパートナーのままで責任も残ります）。また §503(a)(2) により、譲渡それ自体はパートナーの脱退やパートナーシップの解散を生じさせません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.3

questions.stem:
Unless otherwise provided in a general partnership agreement, which of the following statements is correct when a partner dies?

I. The deceased partner's executor would automatically become a partner.
II. The deceased partner's estate would be free from any partnership liabilities.
III. The partner would be dissociated from the partnership automatically.

Executor is partner (I) | Estate free of liability (II) | Dissociated (III)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes | No

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No | Yes

questions.explanation:
Under RUPA §601(7)(i), a partner who is an individual is dissociated from the partnership upon the partner's death, so dissociation occurs automatically (Yes).

The executor does not automatically become a partner (No). Admission as a partner requires the consent of all the partners (RUPA §401(i)); the deceased partner's estate is entitled only to the partner's transferable interest, that is, distributions or a buyout of the interest (RUPA §701). The estate is not free from partnership liabilities (No). Dissociation does not by itself discharge a partner's liability for partnership obligations incurred before dissociation (RUPA §703(a)), so the estate remains liable for obligations that arose while the deceased was a partner.

The combination is therefore No | No | Yes. The combinations stating that the executor would automatically become a partner, or that the estate would be free from any partnership liabilities, are wrong for the reasons above, and the combination stating that the partner would not be dissociated ignores RUPA §601(7)(i).
questions.explanationJa:
RUPA §601(7)(i) により、個人のパートナーは死亡によって自動的にパートナーシップから脱退（dissociation）します（III は Yes）。

遺言執行者が自動的にパートナーになることはありません（I は No）。パートナーとしての加入には全パートナーの同意が必要で（§401(i)）、遺産が受け取れるのは譲渡可能な持分（分配金や持分の買取代金、§701）だけです。また、遺産がパートナーシップ債務から解放されることもありません（II は No）。脱退しても、脱退前に生じた債務についての責任は消えないため（§703(a)）、死亡したパートナーの在任中に生じた債務については遺産が責任を負います。

したがって組合せは No | No | Yes です。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.4

questions.stem:
Cobb, Inc., a partner in TLC Partnership, assigns its partnership interest to Bean, who is not made a partner. After the assignment, Bean asserts the rights to

I. Participate in the management of TLC.
II. Cobb's share of TLC's partnership profits.

Bean is correct as to which of these rights?

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation:
Under RUPA §503(b), the transferee of a partner's transferable interest is entitled to receive, in accordance with the transfer, the distributions to which the transferor would otherwise be entitled. Bean therefore is correct as to the right to Cobb's share of TLC's profits (II).

Bean is not correct as to participating in the management of TLC (I). Because Bean was not made a partner, Bean has no right to participate in the management or conduct of the partnership business or to access partnership records (RUPA §503(a)(3)); management rights belong only to partners (RUPA §401(f)), and Cobb remains the partner. Accordingly, the answers that include the right to participate in management (I only, Both I and II) are wrong, and Neither I nor II is wrong because the right to profits does pass to Bean.
questions.explanationJa:
RUPA §503(b) により、パートナーの譲渡可能な持分の譲受人は、譲渡人が受け取るはずだった分配を受け取る権利を持ちます。したがって、Cobb の利益の分配を受ける権利（II）について Bean の主張は正しいです。

一方、TLC の経営に参加する権利（I）は認められません。Bean はパートナーとして加入していないため、経営への参加権も帳簿閲覧権もありません（§503(a)(3)）。経営権はパートナーだけのもので（§401(f)）、パートナーは引き続き Cobb です。よって正しいのは II だけです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.5

questions.stem:
Downs, Frey, and Vick formed the DFV general partnership to act as manufacturers' representatives. The partners agreed Downs would receive 40% of any partnership profits and Frey and Vick would each receive 30% of such profits. It was also agreed that the partnership would not terminate for five years. After the fourth year, the partners agreed to terminate the partnership. At that time, the partners' capital accounts were as follows: Downs, $20,000; Frey, $15,000; and Vick, $10,000. There also were undistributed losses of $30,000.

Which of the following statements is (are) usually correct regarding general partners' liability?

I. All general partners are jointly and severally liable for partnership torts.
II. All general partners are liable only for those partnership obligations they actually authorized.

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation:
Under RUPA §306(a), all partners are liable jointly and severally for all obligations of the partnership, including obligations arising from torts committed by a partner or employee acting in the ordinary course of the partnership's business (RUPA §305). Statement I is therefore correct. (Under RUPA §307(d), a judgment creditor generally must first exhaust partnership assets before levying on a partner's personal assets, but the partners' liability is still joint and several.)

Statement II is incorrect. A general partner is an agent of the partnership, and the partnership is bound by any partner's act for apparently carrying on the partnership business in the ordinary course (RUPA §301(1)). Because every partner is personally liable for all partnership obligations, liability is not limited to obligations a partner actually authorized. Accordingly, II only, Both I and II, and Neither I nor II are wrong.
questions.explanationJa:
RUPA §306(a) により、パートナーは全員がパートナーシップのすべての債務について連帯して（jointly and severally）責任を負います。通常の業務の中でパートナーや従業員が行った不法行為による債務も含まれます（§305）。したがって I は正しいです。（§307(d) により、判決債権者は原則としてまずパートナーシップの財産から回収する必要がありますが、それでも責任は連帯責任です。）

II は誤りです。一般パートナーはパートナーシップの代理人であり、通常の業務の範囲で行ったパートナーの行為にはパートナーシップが拘束されます（§301(1)）。各パートナーはパートナーシップの全債務について個人責任を負うので、自分が実際に承認した債務だけに責任が限られることはありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.6

questions.stem:
Downs, Frey, and Vick formed the DFV general partnership to act as manufacturers' representatives. The partners agreed Downs would receive 40% of any partnership profits and Frey and Vick would each receive 30% of such profits. It was also agreed that the partnership would not terminate for five years. After the fourth year, the partners agreed to terminate the partnership. At that time, the partners' capital accounts were as follows: Downs, $20,000; Frey, $15,000; and Vick, $10,000. There also were undistributed losses of $30,000.

Vick's share of the undistributed losses will be
questions.explanation:
Under RUPA §401(b), each partner is chargeable with a share of the partnership losses in proportion to the partner's share of the profits, unless the partners agree otherwise. The partners agreed only on a profit ratio (40% / 30% / 30%) and made no separate agreement on losses, so losses are shared in the same ratio.

Vick's share of losses = $30,000 × 30% = $9,000.

$0 is wrong because a general partner must bear a share of partnership losses. $10,000 is wrong because it divides the losses equally among the three partners ($30,000 ÷ 3); equal sharing applies only when there is no agreement on profits, and here there is a profit-sharing agreement. $1,000 has no basis; it equals Vick's $10,000 capital account less the $9,000 loss share, which is Vick's remaining capital, not the share of losses.
questions.explanationJa:
RUPA §401(b) により、別段の合意が無ければ、各パートナーは利益の分配割合と同じ割合で損失を負担します。本問では利益の分配割合（40%／30%／30%）だけが合意され、損失の負担割合の定めは無いので、損失も同じ割合で負担します。

Vick の損失負担額 = $30,000 × 30% = $9,000

$0 は誤りで、一般パートナーは損失の負担を免れません。$10,000 は3人で均等に分けた額（$30,000 ÷ 3）ですが、均等分配になるのは利益の分配について合意が無い場合だけです。$1,000 は Vick の出資勘定 $10,000 から損失負担 $9,000 を引いた残額で、損失の負担額ではありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.7

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements regarding a limited partner is (are) generally correct?

I. The limited partner is subject to personal liability for partnership debts.
II. The limited partner has the right to take part in the control of the partnership.

Subject to personal liability (I) | Right to take part in control (II)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
A limited partner is not subject to personal liability for partnership debts (No). Under ULPA (2001) §303, an obligation of a limited partnership is not the obligation of a limited partner solely by reason of being a limited partner; the limited partner's risk is limited to the capital contributed or promised. ULPA (2001) also eliminated the old control rule, so a limited partner does not become personally liable even if the limited partner participates in management.

A limited partner does not have the right to take part in the control of the partnership (No). Under ULPA (2001) §302 and §406, management and control are vested in the general partners, and a limited partner has no right or power, as a limited partner, to act for or bind the partnership; limited partners only consent to certain fundamental matters.

The combination is therefore No | No. Any combination answering Yes for personal liability ignores the limited liability that is the defining feature of a limited partner, and any combination answering Yes for control ignores that control belongs to the general partners.
questions.explanationJa:
有限責任パートナー（limited partner）は、パートナーシップの債務について個人責任を負いません（I は No）。ULPA (2001) §303 により、有限責任パートナーであるというだけでは LP の債務は自分の債務にならず、リスクは出資額（約束した出資額）に限られます。ULPA (2001) は旧法のコントロール・ルールを廃止したため、経営に関与しても個人責任を負うことはありません。

また、有限責任パートナーには LP の経営を支配する権利もありません（II は No）。§302・§406 により、経営は一般パートナー（general partner）が行い、有限責任パートナーはその立場で LP を代理・拘束する権限を持ちません。同意権があるのは一部の基本的事項だけです。

したがって組合せは No | No です。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.8

questions.stem: Unless otherwise provided in the limited partnership agreement, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A general partner's capital contribution may not consist of services rendered to the partnership.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Upon the death of a limited partner, the partnership will be dissolved.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A person may own a limited partnership interest in the same partnership in which s/he is a general partner.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Upon the assignment of a limited partner's interest, the assignee will become a substituted limited partner if the consent of two-thirds of all partners is obtained.

questions.explanation:
Under ULPA (2001) §113, a person may be both a general partner and a limited partner in the same limited partnership. That person has the rights, powers, duties, and obligations of a general partner and, separately, the rights of a limited partner with respect to the limited partnership interest.

The statement that a general partner's contribution may not consist of services is wrong: a contribution may be property or a benefit to the partnership, including services performed or a promise to perform services (ULPA (2001) §102(2), §501). The statement that the partnership is dissolved upon the death of a limited partner is wrong; the death causes only the dissociation of that limited partner (ULPA (2001) §601(b)(6)), and the partnership continues. The statement that the assignee becomes a substituted limited partner with the consent of two-thirds of all partners is wrong; absent a provision in the partnership agreement, a transferee becomes a limited partner only with the consent of all the partners (ULPA (2001) §301(3)).
questions.explanationJa:
ULPA (2001) §113 により、同じ LP で一般パートナーと有限責任パートナーを兼ねることができます。その者は一般パートナーとしての権利義務を持ち、それとは別に、保有する有限責任パートナー持分について有限責任パートナーの権利を持ちます。

「一般パートナーの出資は役務提供では認められない」は誤りで、出資には役務の提供やその約束も含まれます（§102(2)・§501）。「有限責任パートナーの死亡で LP は解散する」も誤りで、死亡によってその有限責任パートナーが脱退するだけで、LP は存続します（§601(b)(6)）。「パートナーの3分の2の同意で譲受人は代替の有限責任パートナーになる」も誤りで、契約に定めが無ければ、譲受人が有限責任パートナーになるには全パートナーの同意が必要です（§301(3)）。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.9

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the membership of a limited liability company?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An LLC must have at least two members.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An LLC may be managed by either a member or by a non-member manager.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All members of an LLC must be U.S. citizens or resident aliens.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trusts cannot be members of an LLC, but corporations and partnerships can be.

questions.explanation:
Under RULLCA §407, an LLC is member-managed unless the operating agreement provides that it is manager-managed. In a manager-managed LLC, the managers need not be members, so an LLC may be managed by its members or by a non-member manager.

The statement that an LLC must have at least two members is wrong; every state permits single-member LLCs. The statement that all members must be U.S. citizens or resident aliens is wrong; that type of shareholder restriction applies to S corporations (IRC §1361(b)), not to LLCs, which may have foreign individuals or entities as members. The statement that trusts cannot be members is wrong; any person, including an individual, corporation, partnership, trust, or estate, may be an LLC member (RULLCA §102 definition of person).
questions.explanationJa:
RULLCA §407 により、LLC は運営契約で manager-managed と定めない限り member-managed です。manager-managed の LLC ではマネージャーはメンバーである必要が無いので、メンバーが経営しても、メンバーでないマネージャーが経営してもかまいません。

「LLC は2人以上のメンバーが必要」は誤りで、どの州でも1人の LLC（single-member LLC）が認められます。「メンバーは全員が米国市民か居住外国人でなければならない」も誤りで、それは S 法人の株主要件（IRC §1361(b)）です。LLC のメンバーには外国人や外国の事業体もなれます。「信託はメンバーになれない」も誤りで、個人・法人・パートナーシップ・信託・遺産など、どの「者」もメンバーになれます。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.10

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the tax status of a limited liability company?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A multi-member LLC is treated as an association taxable as a corporation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A single-member LLC is treated in the same manner as an S corporation with a sole shareholder.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When one member of an LLC with two members dies, the LLC automatically terminates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a single-member LLC admits a new member, the entity is treated as a partnership for tax purposes.

questions.explanation:
Under the check-the-box regulations (Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3(b)(1)), absent an election, a domestic eligible entity with two or more members is classified as a partnership, and a single-member entity is disregarded as separate from its owner. Under Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3(f)(2), when a disregarded single-member LLC admits a new member, it becomes an entity with two members and is classified as a partnership by default (see Rev. Rul. 99-5).

The statement that a multi-member LLC is treated as an association taxable as a corporation is wrong; that is true only if the LLC elects corporate classification on Form 8832, and the default is partnership treatment. The statement that a single-member LLC is treated like an S corporation is wrong; by default it is a disregarded entity (reported, for example, on the individual owner's Schedule C), and S corporation status requires an election. The statement that the LLC automatically terminates when one of two members dies is wrong; under RULLCA §602 and §701, a member's death causes dissociation, not dissolution of the LLC.
questions.explanationJa:
チェック・ザ・ボックス規則（Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3(b)(1)）により、選択をしない場合、メンバーが2人以上の国内 LLC はパートナーシップとして、1人の LLC は所有者と一体の disregarded entity として扱われます。1人の LLC が新しいメンバーを迎えると2人の事業体になり、原則どおりパートナーシップとして扱われます（§301.7701-3(f)(2)、Rev. Rul. 99-5）。

「複数メンバーの LLC は法人として課税される」は誤りで、Form 8832 で法人課税を選択した場合だけです。「1人の LLC は株主1人の S 法人と同じ扱い」も誤りで、原則は disregarded entity（個人所有なら Schedule C で申告）であり、S 法人になるには選択が必要です。「2人の LLC でメンバー1人が死亡すると LLC は自動的に終了する」も誤りで、RULLCA §602・§701 により、死亡はそのメンバーの脱退事由にすぎず、LLC の解散事由ではありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.11

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the operating characteristics of a limited liability company (LLC)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An LLC may operate only in the state in which it is organized.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Since an LLC is an American legal entity, it cannot conduct operations outside of the United States.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In general, unless restricted by state law, an LLC can conduct any lawful activity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An LLC may engage only in state-regulated professional activities (such as accounting, law, medicine, actuarial science, architecture, and engineering).

questions.explanation:
Under RULLCA §104(b), a limited liability company may have any lawful purpose, regardless of whether for profit. Some states restrict particular activities (for example, banking or insurance) or impose special rules on professional LLCs, but in general an LLC can conduct any lawful activity.

The statement that an LLC may operate only in its state of organization is wrong; an LLC may do business in other states by registering there as a foreign LLC (RULLCA §902). The statement that an LLC cannot conduct operations outside the United States is wrong; nothing in the statute limits an LLC's activities to the United States. The statement that an LLC may engage only in state-regulated professional activities is wrong; professional services are one permitted use of the LLC form (often as a professional LLC), but LLCs may engage in any lawful business.
questions.explanationJa:
RULLCA §104(b) により、LLC は営利か否かを問わず、あらゆる適法な目的を持つことができます。銀行・保険など一部の業種を州法が制限したり、専門職の LLC に特別な規制を置いたりすることはありますが、原則として LLC はどんな適法な事業も行えます。

「設立した州でしか事業ができない」は誤りで、他州で外国 LLC として登録すれば事業を行えます（§902）。「米国の事業体なので米国外では事業ができない」も誤りで、事業地を米国内に限る規定はありません。「州が規制する専門職の事業しかできない」も誤りで、専門職は LLC の利用方法の一つにすぎず、LLC は適法な事業なら何でも営めます。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.12

questions.stem: Under the Revised Model Business Corporation Act, which of the following must be contained in a corporation's articles of incorporation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Quorum voting requirements

choices.label: B
choices.text: Names of stockholders

choices.label: C
choices.text: Provisions for issuance of par and nonpar shares

choices.label: D
choices.text: The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue

questions.explanation:
RMBCA §2.02(a) lists the mandatory contents of the articles of incorporation: (1) a corporate name, (2) the number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue, (3) the street address of the initial registered office and the name of the initial registered agent, and (4) the name and address of each incorporator. The number of authorized shares is therefore required.

Quorum voting requirements are optional; they may be set in the articles or bylaws, and otherwise the statutory default (a majority of the votes entitled to be cast) applies (RMBCA §2.02(b), §7.25). Names of stockholders are not required; the articles name the incorporators, not the shareholders, and shareholder names appear in the corporation's share records. Provisions for issuance of par and nonpar shares are optional under RMBCA §2.02(b); the RMBCA does not require par value at all.
questions.explanationJa:
RMBCA §2.02(a) が定める定款の必要的記載事項は、(1) 会社の名称、(2) 発行可能株式総数、(3) 当初の登録事務所の所在地と登録代理人の氏名、(4) 各発起人の氏名・住所 の4つです。したがって発行可能株式総数は必ず記載します。

定足数の要件は任意的記載事項で、定款や付属定款（bylaws）で定めなければ法律の原則（議決権の過半数）が適用されます（§2.02(b)・§7.25）。株主の氏名は不要で、定款に載るのは発起人であり、株主は株主名簿で管理されます。額面株式・無額面株式の発行に関する定めも任意で（§2.02(b)）、RMBCA はそもそも額面を要求していません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.13

questions.stem: Case Corp. is incorporated in State A. Under the Revised Model Business Corporation Act, which of the following activities engaged in by Case requires that Case obtain a certificate of authority to do business in State B?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maintaining bank accounts in State B.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Collecting corporate debts in State B.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hiring employees who are residents of State B.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maintaining an office in State B to conduct intrastate business.

questions.explanation:
Under RMBCA §15.01(a), a foreign corporation may not transact business in a state until it obtains a certificate of authority (registers) there. Maintaining an office in State B to conduct intrastate business is regular, continuous business activity within State B, so Case must qualify there.

RMBCA §15.01(b) lists activities that do not constitute transacting business, including maintaining accounts in financial institutions and securing or collecting debts. Maintaining bank accounts in State B and collecting corporate debts in State B therefore do not require a certificate of authority. Hiring employees who are residents of State B also does not by itself require one; the residence of the employees says nothing about whether Case conducts intrastate business in State B (for example, the employees may work at Case's office in State A or engage only in interstate commerce, which §15.01(b) also excludes).
questions.explanationJa:
RMBCA §15.01(a) により、外国法人（他州で設立された会社）は、その州で営業許可（certificate of authority）を得るまで事業を行えません。州内取引のために B 州に事務所を置くことは、B 州内で継続的に事業を行うことに当たるので、Case は B 州で許可を取る必要があります。

§15.01(b) は「事業を行うことに当たらない行為」として、金融機関に口座を持つこと、債権の担保取得や回収などを挙げています。したがって B 州に銀行口座を持つことや、B 州で債権を回収することには許可は不要です。B 州の住民を従業員として雇うことも、それだけでは B 州内で事業を行うことにはなりません（従業員が A 州の事務所で働く場合や、§15.01(b) が除外する州際取引だけに従事する場合もあります）。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Business Entities Q.14

questions.stem: Price owns 2,000 shares of Universal Corp.'s $10 cumulative preferred stock. During its first year of operations, cash dividends of $5 per share were declared on the preferred stock but were never paid. In the second year, dividends on the preferred stock were neither declared nor paid. If Universal is dissolved, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Universal will be liable to Price as an unsecured creditor for $10,000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Universal will be liable to Price as a secured creditor for $20,000.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Price will have priority over the claims of Universal's bond owners.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Price will have priority over the claims of Universal's unsecured judgment creditors.

questions.explanation:
Once a cash dividend is declared, it becomes a debt of the corporation, and the shareholder is an unsecured creditor for the declared but unpaid amount (see RMBCA §6.40(f), which treats a distribution indebtedness as on a parity with the corporation's general, unsecured creditors). Dividends that have not been declared are not a debt, even on cumulative preferred stock; the arrearage gives the preferred shareholder only a priority over common shareholders in future distributions and liquidation.
